newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: AUSTRALIAN PM SAYS TO LOOK AT BROAD-BASED TAX.
newsitem.headline: AUSTRALIAN PM SAYS TO LOOK AT BROAD-BASED TAX.

text.p: Australian Prime Minister John Howard said on Wednesday the government would consider the introduction of a broad-based indirect tax.
""Consideration should be given, of course, to a broad-based indirect tax to replace some or all of the existing indirect taxes," Howard told reporters.

Howard began the push for Australia's taxation system to be overhauled in May when he said there was a need for a debate on the issue. He also revamped a campaign for a controversial goods and services tax (GST) -- a broad-based consumption tax paid when a consumer buys a good or service -- that many blame for delaying the Liberal-National coalition's return to power.
The coalition, which lost what was regarded as an unloseable election in 1993 with a policy for a GST, pledged in the 1996 election not to introduce a consumption tax in its first three-year term.
But community support for a GST has grown in recent months and Howard has not ruled out its introduction in the government's second term.
Howard said options for a broad-based indirect tax remained numerous and he was not committed to any one type at this stage.
"I'm not particularly wedded to a particular form of a broad-based indirect tax or a particular description of one," he said.
